The new transport carries those requests from a remote Codex host to the existing Gateway relay owner. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Remote callback configuration] --> B[Codex plugin] B --> C[Scoped credential file] C --> D[Native child hook command] D --> E[Gateway HTTPS callback] E --> F[Token and live owner checks] F --> G[Existing hook policy] G --> H[Allow or deny result] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

This establishes file-level release absence, not a claim that every remote deployment scenario was tested. ([fc23bc864e45](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943)) - **Callback authority chain:** The callback checks the relay token, provider and target, registration identity before and after awaiting the body, and exact remote generation. Invocation then uses the existing foreground or retained-child authority checks, including revalidation after asynchronous policy work before returning an allow result. ([`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-bridge.ts:293`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5d928aadf5e386e0a8ae1dab9cff0c7b9797052/src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-bridge.ts#L293), [d5d928aadf5e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d5d928aadf5e386e0a8ae1dab9cff0c7b9797052)) - **Credential lifecycle and compatibility:** Credential projection serializes writes and removals, captures the app-server client, checks current authority before delivery, and prevents an old projection from deleting its successor. The remote option is additive; absent configuration retains the local transport. No existing authoritative stored-data schema or format is rewritten. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay-remote.ts:50`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5d928aadf5e386e0a8ae1dab9cff0c7b9797052/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay-remote.ts#L50), [d5d928aadf5e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d5d928aadf5e386e0a8ae1dab9cff0c7b9797052)) - **Recorded deployment evidence and accepted trust scope:** The captured PR body reports a deployed run at 43a7333aa04c30c232877956bbdcd330d85c771c with stock Codex 0.160.0: native spawn/wait/result, a successful child command, inherited developer instructions, and a subsequent parent turn. It also reports deployed HTTPS rejection of invalid tokens, target mismatches, stale generations, and retired capabilities with 403/410 outcomes. The maintain-access author's stated design explicitly accepts that the Harness OS user can read its own restricted hook credential; it grants no operator RPC authority. Kubernetes and AWS rollout coverage is expressly unclaimed. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

The data-model migration checklist is not applicable to this change. In `extensions/codex/src/app-server/protocol.ts`, the only additions are TypeScript request contracts for `fs/writeFile` and `fs/remove`; neither is persisted application state. Both RPCs and these fields already exist in stock Codex 0.160.0 ([protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L977), [request types](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/fs.rs#L28)).

The new credential file is a disposable projection owned by a live relay generation, written on preparation and removed on retirement. No existing database schema, session record, or authoritative stored format changes. Without the opt-in callback configuration, the existing local transport is retained. The recorded full local deployment used the unchanged Codex 0.160.0 binary and exercised this write/remove path. This agrees with the review’s own compatibility evidence that no authoritative stored-data format is rewritten.

Disposition: no migration or migration code is required. Current-head required CI is green, and the completed review reports no actionable code or security findings.
